title: Combined Metagenomic / Metatranscriptomic Pipeline for Host-associated Microbiomes
author: Scott Daniel
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.d7m9k5

steps.title: Clone sample data repository
steps.instruction: Clone the mg‑sample‑data repository from GitHub using: `git clone https://github.com/hurwitzlab/mg-sample-data.git`. The dataset is < 10 MB and can be placed on a shared supercomputer, a job‑scheduler‑managed directory, or a local laptop.

steps.title: Clone FastQC Singularity recipe
steps.instruction: Clone the Singularity recipe that contains FastQC and SolexaQA with: `git clone https://github.com/hurwitzlab/singularity-fastqc.git`. This must be done on a system where you have sudo privileges.

steps.title: Build FastQC Singularity image
steps.instruction: Enter the cloned directory and run the build script: `cd singularity-fastqc && ./create_and_bootstrap.sh`. The script should create a file named `fastqc.img`. Verify that no error appears (e.g., "ABORT: Aborting with RETVAL=255").

steps.title: Transfer FastQC image
steps.instruction: Copy the resulting `fastqc.img` to a directory on your shared supercomputer (or any directory that is in your `$PATH`, such as `/bin`) using `scp` or `sftp`.

steps.title: Generate FastQC quality reports (optional)
steps.instruction: Run the provided FastQC reporting script: `mg-sample-data/scripts/00-fastqc-reports.sh`. Submit it to a PBS scheduler with `./00-fastqc-reports.sh` (or edit `./workers/fastqc.sh` for another scheduler). For manual execution, run the worker script directly: `scripts/workers/fastqc.sh`.

steps.title: Run Trim Galore on reads
steps.instruction: Execute the Trim Galore wrapper (which calls cutadapt) to trim low‑quality bases and adapters. Use the example script: `mg-sample-data/scripts/01-trim-galore.sh` and submit it to a PBS job array with `./01-trim-galore.sh`. Edit `./workers/trimgalore.sh` if you use a different scheduler. The default trimming stops when the probability that a base call is correct reaches 99 % or greater.

steps.title: Compare pre‑ and post‑trim reports
steps.instruction: Inspect the FastQC reports generated before step 5 and after step 6. If the quality improvement is minimal, consider re‑running Trim Galore with different parameters.

steps.title: Clone Tuxedo and Taxoner recipes
steps.instruction: Clone the Singularity recipes for the Tuxedo suite and Taxoner: `git clone https://github.com/hurwitzlab/singularity-tuxedo.git` and `git clone https://github.com/hurwitzlab/singularity-taxoner.git`.

steps.title: Build Bowtie/Cufflinks image
steps.instruction: Enter the Tuxedo directory and run the build script: `cd singularity-tuxedo && ./create_and_bootstrap.sh`. This creates `bowcuff.img`. Confirm that no error such as "ABORT: Aborting with RETVAL=255" occurs.

steps.title: Build Taxoner Singularity image
steps.instruction: Enter the Taxoner directory and run: `cd singularity-taxoner && ./create_and_bootstrap.sh`. This creates `taxoner.img`. Verify that the script finishes without the abort error.

steps.title: Transfer Bowtie and Taxoner images
steps.instruction: Copy `bowcuff.img` and `taxoner.img` to a directory on your shared supercomputer or to any location in your `$PATH` (e.g., `/bin`) using `scp` or `sftp`.

steps.title: Prepare taxonomy database for Bowtie2
steps.instruction: Submit the PBS script that builds the lineage file and genome FASTA files needed for Bowtie2 indexing: `mg-sample-data/scripts/02-taxadb-prep.pbs`. Use `qsub 02-taxadb-prep.pbs` (or edit for another scheduler).

steps.title: Build Bowtie2 indices from split FASTA
steps.instruction: Run the Bowtie2 index‑building script: `mg-sample-data/scripts/03-bowtie2-build.sh`. Submit it with `./03-bowtie2-build.sh` (or edit `./workers/bowtie2-build.sh` for another scheduler). The script expects the multi‑genome FASTA to be split into ~4 GB files so that indexing can be parallelised across multiple computers.

steps.title: Edit configuration variables
steps.instruction: Open `config.sh` in your preferred text editor and set the required directory paths and other variables for the pipeline.

steps.title: Clone Centrifuge Singularity recipe
steps.instruction: If you plan to use Centrifuge for species identification, clone its recipe: `git clone https://github.com/scottdaniel/singularity-centrifuge.git`. You may optionally skip the QC and Bowtie2 preparation steps when using this classifier.

steps.title: Build Centrifuge Singularity image
steps.instruction: Enter the Centrifuge directory and build the image with: `cd singularity-centrifuge && make img`.

steps.title: Run Taxoner on DNA reads
steps.instruction: Execute the Taxoner script to determine species composition of the DNA reads: `mg-sample-data/scripts/04-taxoner.sh`. Submit it to PBS with `./04-taxoner.sh` (or edit `./workers/runTaxoner.sh` for another scheduler).
